text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.37% today, continuing a modest upward drift over the past week as oil prices have climbed sharply. U.S. crude hit $97.26 a barrel today—above $100 earlier this week—driven by escalating U.S.-Iran tensions that threaten Middle East supply. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits when crude prices rise, since higher oil fetches more revenue per barrel pumped and sold.

The stock's 4.92% gain over two weeks reflects the broader market repricing of energy as geopolitical risk keeps crude elevated. Market participants are betting that Middle East supply disruptions will persist through at least the midterm elections, according to recent commentary, which means sustained pricing power for established oil producers like ConocoPhillips.
